content: 1. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of apomorphine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of arformoterol by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Azithromycin enhances the effects of argatroban by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Both aripiprazole and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 5. Both arsenic trioxide and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Both artemether and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Azithromycin and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of asenapine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Both asenapine transdermal and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Both atomoxetine and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 11. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of atorvastatin by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. If used together, monitor for atorvastatin toxicity (e.g., muscle aches, renal dysfunction). 12. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of balsalazide by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 14. Azithromycin decreases the effects of the BCG vaccine live by pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live bacterial vaccines. 15. Azithromycin and bedaquiline both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended. 16. Azithromycin increases the effects of bemiparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Azithromycin increases the levels of berotralstat by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Azithromycin increases the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Reduce the betrixaban dose to 80 mg PO once, then 40 mg PO daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. 19. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of biotin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Azithromycin increases the effects of bivalirudin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Both buprenorphine and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Both buprenorphine buccal and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Both buprenorphine subdermal implant and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Both buprenorphine transdermal and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Both buprenorphine long-acting injection and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of azithromycin by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. Separate administration by 2 hours. 27. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefdinir by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 28. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefditoren by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 29. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefoxitin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 30. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefpodoxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 31. Azithromycin decreases the effects of cefuroxime by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Bacteriostatic agents may inhibit the effects of bactericidal agents. 32. Azithromycin increases the levels of ceritinib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. 33. Both ceritinib and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of cetirizine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Chloroquine increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval, and azithromycin increases the toxicity of chloroquine by prolonging the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 36. Both chlorpromazine and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Azithromycin decreases the effects of the cholera vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of the cholera vaccine with systemic antibiotics, as these agents may be active against the vaccine strain. Do not administer the cholera vaccine to patients who have received oral or parenteral antibiotics within 14 days prior to vaccination. 38. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of cisapride by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Both azithromycin and citalopram prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. ECG monitoring is recommended, along with caution when using drugs that may prolong the QT interval. 41. Both azithromycin and clarithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of clofazimine by prolonging the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 43. Both clomipramine and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Both clozapine and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 45. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of clozapine through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Enhanced CNS toxicity may occur. 46. Both cobicistat and azithromycin increase the levels of each other by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Consider alternative antibiotics when cobicistat is coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. 47. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of colchicine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid colchicine with P-gp inhibitors. If coadministration is necessary, decrease colchicine dose or frequency as recommended in prescribing information. Use of colchicine with P-gp inhibitors is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. 48. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of conjugated estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 49. Both crizotinib and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of crizotinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of cyclosporine by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of dabigatran by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. For atrial fibrillation, avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl < 30 mL/min. For DVT/PE treatment, avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl < 50 mL/min. 52. Azithromycin increases the effects of dalteparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 53. Both azithromycin and dasatinib prolong the QTc interval. Minor significance; clinical relevance is unknown. 54. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of degarelix by prolonging the QTc interval. Minor significance; clinical relevance is unknown. 55. Both desflurane and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 56. Both desipramine and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of deutetrabenazine by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. At the maximum recommended dose, deutetrabenazine does not prolong the QT interval to a clinically relevant extent. Certain circumstances may increase the risk of torsade de pointes or sudden death in association with drugs that prolong the QTc interval (e.g., bradycardia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, coadministration with other QT-prolonging drugs, congenital QT prolongation). 58. Both dichlorphenamide and azithromycin decrease serum potassium. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Azithromycin decreases the effects of dicloxacillin by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Minor significance; clinical relevance is unknown. 60. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of dienogest/estradiol valerate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor closely. An alternate or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 61. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of digoxin by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 62. Both azithromycin and disopyramide prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 63. Both azithromycin and dofetilide prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Dofetilide increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. 64. Both azithromycin and dolasetron prolong the QTc interval. Minor significance; clinical relevance is unknown. 65. Both donepezil and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 66. Both doxepin and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Both azithromycin and dronedarone prolong the QTc interval. This combination is contraindicated. Concomitant use may increase the risk of QT prolongation and cardiac arrhythmias. 68. Both azithromycin and droperidol prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of duvelisib by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of edoxaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Dose adjustment may be required with strong P-gp inhibitors. For DVT/PE treatment, decrease the dose to 30 mg PO once daily. For NVAF, no dose reduction is recommended. 71. Both efavirenz and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 72. Both eliglustat and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 73. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of encorafenib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Azithromycin increases the effects of enoxaparin by decreasing its metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 75. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of entrectinib by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 76. Both epinephrine and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 77. Both racemic epinephrine and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 78. Azithromycin increases the levels of ergotamine by an unknown mechanism. Minor significance; clinical relevance is unknown. 79. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of eribulin by prolonging the QTc interval. Minor significance; clinical relevance is unknown. 80. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of erythromycin base by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both azithromycin and erythromycin base prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 81. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of erythromycin ethylsuccinate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both azithromycin and erythromycin ethylsuccinate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 82. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of erythromycin lactobionate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both azithromycin and erythromycin lactobionate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 83. Azithromycin increases the level or effect of erythromycin stearate by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Both azithromycin and erythromycin stearate prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 84. Azithromycin increases the toxicity of escitalopram by prolonging the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Escitalopram increases the toxicity of azithromycin by prolonging the QTc interval. 85. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 86. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of conjugated synthetic estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 87. Azithromycin decreases the level or effect of estropipate by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 88. Both ezogabine and azithromycin increase the toxicity of each other by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Slight and transient QT prolongation has been observed with ezogabine, particularly when titrated to 1200 mg/day. QT interval monitoring is recommended when ezogabine is prescribed with agents known to prolong the QT interval. 89. Both fexinidazole and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration of fexinidazole with drugs known to block potassium channels or prolong the QT interval. 90. Both fingolimod and azithromycin prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug.
